Logan —

I reviewed the customer redlines and sketched positions below (short form). I also annotated the attached doc with comments (see Drive link in related_links).

1) Effective dates / sequencing: Acceptable approach — we sign MSA now with a short declarative clause that the order form governs billing and capacity only when executed. Then include an express statement that order form effective date is 2028-08-01. This protects both sides and preserves your commercial ask. Rationale: avoids having two conflicting "effective" dates while keeping their operational requirement.

2) Liability cap carve: Push back on a carve that excludes costs for gross negligence. Standard cap applies; we can agree narrow carve for third-party PCI fines only if they show specific regulatory exposure. Rationale: unlimited carve materially increases risk.

3) Burst capacity clause: Accept in principle but convert to a defined mechanism: "Customer may request up to X additional nodes (describe pricing) with 30 days' notice; Redwood will confirm availability and pricing within 5 business days." We'll add a one-time provisioning lead time and an optional prorated charge.

4) Order-form start date mismatch: Propose we set order-form effective 2028-08-01 and allow a provisioning window starting 08/01 but billing to begin 09/01 only if they insist. This is often an acceptable compromise where operations gets time to stand up nodes but finance retains a clean billing period.

5) Indemnity language & data breach: Tighten definitions and keep mutual indemnities for third-party claims. For data incidents, suggest a middle-ground: Redwood remains responsible for direct damages caused by proven negligence; both parties remove wording that implies subjection to unlimited statutory fines.

If you want, I can draft redline language for sections: 2.1 (term), 6.2 (liability cap), 8.4 (burst capacity), and 12.1 (indemnity). Also note: HubSpot deal 2049 has the capacity uplift and the pricing SKU changes; Marcus/ Lauren I'll need the final SKU mapping so I can reference exact numbers in the redline.

-Karthik

Hi Marta / Skyforge Legal —

Thank you for the redlines and context. Per our internal review (summary below) we can move forward if the following positions are acceptable to you: 

1) Sequencing: Redwood will execute the MSA upon signature. We will execute the Order Form with an explicit effective date 2028-08-01. The order form will include a provisioning window that allows operational setup starting 08/01. This ensures your procurement requirement (MSA in place) and our billing clarity.

2) Liability cap carve: We cannot accept a carve that removes liability caps for gross negligence. Instead Redwood will accept a limited carve for verified regulatory fines where Redwood directly failed to maintain controls (we will propose narrow language).

3) Burst capacity: We will add a clause that allows Skyforge to request up to 20% additional nodes (billing as a separate SKU) with 30 days' notice; Redwood will confirm availability in 5 business days. If you need a higher committed uplift we can include a reserve pricing table.

4) Order-form start date: We propose 2028-08-01 as the order-form effective date. Billing will begin 2028-09-01 unless Skyforge confirms they want billing to start on 08/01; if so we will prorate the first month.
